entries.proposition: NHP GLP design: single ICM dose in juvenile rhesus macaques, vehicle n=2 and three dose groups of n=6, no immune suppression, half euthanised at 3 and half at 6 months.
entries.snippet: without immune-suppression treatment. We euthanized half of the animals at 3 months postdosing and the other half at 6 months postdosing.
entries.anchor: Results, ICM AAVhu68.hGALCco is well tolerated in NHPs, para 1

entries.proposition: Doses: 4.5E12, 1.5E13 and 4.5E13 genome copies (5.0E10, 1.7E11 and 5.0E11 GC per gram brain).
Dog arm: seven dogs, four AAV-treated Krabbe dogs, one ICM dose of 3.0E13 GC in 1 mL, no immune suppression or anti-inflammatory regimen.
entries.snippet: The dogs did not receive any immune suppression or anti-inflammatory regimen.

entries.proposition: DRG finding in NHP: minimal sporadic degeneration of DRG sensory neurons with secondary axonopathy.
entries.snippet: Test article administration resulted in minimal sporadic degeneration of primarily DRG sensory neurons, which led to secondary degeneration of associated central and peripheral axons (i.e., axonopathy).

entries.proposition: DRG lesions were absent in some treated animals and minimal when present; axonopathy minimal to mild, with many sections negative.
entries.snippet: The DRG lesions were absent in some test article-treated animals and were minimal in severity when present.

entries.proposition: Text: secondary axonopathy minimal to mild when present, many sections with no finding.
entries.snippet: Secondary axonopathy associated with DRG lesions was minimal to mild when present, with many sections showing no findings

entries.proposition: Axonopathy was dose dependent, most in the high-dose group.
entries.snippet: The secondary dorsal axonopathy was dose dependent, with the HD group showing the most histological findings

entries.proposition: Findings were stable between 90 and 180 days.
entries.snippet: The incidence and severity were similar at days 90 and 180, showing a lack of pathology progression

entries.proposition: One high-dose animal had a large fall in median-nerve sensory action potential, with a grade 3 dorsal column axonopathy.
entries.snippet: decreased SNAPs from the left median nerve (amplitude down from 23.2 μV baseline to 6.6 μV) in one HD animal

entries.proposition: Severity scale used for the DRG and axonopathy grades.
entries.snippet: (0 = normal, 1 = minimal, 2 = mild, 3 = moderate, 4 = marked, and 5 = severe)

entries.proposition: Dog arm: no treatment-related histopathological findings including DRG.
entries.snippet: No test article-related histopathological adverse findings were observed, including in DRG collected from cervical, thoracic, and lumbar regions

entries.proposition: The authors state DRG risk seems low on their NHP and dog data and note the dog is less sensitive than the NHP.
entries.snippet: suggests that dog is less sensitive than NHP

entries.proposition: Figure 5C panel: DRG neuronal degeneration scores never exceed 1 (minimal) at any dose; the dorsal axonopathy panel reaches 3 (moderate) in the high-dose group, which the text sentence 'minimal to mild when present' does not show.
entries.snippet: (0 = normal, 1 = minimal, 2 = mild, 3 = moderate, 4 = marked, and 5 = severe)
entries.anchor: Figure 5C, both plots, read at native resolution
entries.qualifies_needle: Secondary axonopathy associated with DRG lesions was minimal to mild when present
